 Medicare open enrollment is underway: What you need to know
 Caroline Jaime Updated 2026년 10월 25일 일 오전 10:24 UTC 0 ( NewsNation ) — Open enrollment for Medicare is underway, allowing people to change their enrollment before Dec. 7. 
 The decision impacts the costs of medication and medical care for millions of Americans, yet a new poll shows that 60% of older adults spend less than an hour choosing their health plan during open enrollment.
 This year's enrollment selection may be the most important in 25 years, according to University of Michigan health researcher Dr. Mark Fendrick. Policy decisions by the government and changes to insurance agencies that partner with Medicare have had a widespread impact, specifically on prescription drug insurance.
 Who qualifies for Medicare’s new $50-a-month GLP-1 program? 
 What has changed with Medicare drug insurance plans?
 The government has raised the maximum deductible by $85, meaning you could have to pay $700 out of pocket.
 If you are able to take generic medication, you may be able to get refills for free. Pay attention to plans that offer $0 copay for certain medications.
 The cap, or the total amount a person will have to pay out of pocket for prescription drugs, has also risen to $2,400 — $300 higher than in 2026.
 The science and politics behind the panic over ultraprocessed foods 
 Advertisement
 When deciding on a Medicare prescription plan, look at the list of drugs and whether they are covered in the doses you need. Every plan has its own list of drugs and doses, called formularies. If a drug is on multiple lists, you could end up paying more on one plan versus the other depending on the tier it has been ranked.
 Some plans may also require prior permission from a doctor or clinician for covered medications. It's also possible the plan will require your health care provider to provide proof you've tried other drugs first that have not worked, called step therapy.
 In 2027, formularies have listed 25 drugs negotiated with drug companies at a lower out-of-pocket cost. The negotiated price includes all forms and dose levels of those drugs. This price is what the insurance company will pay, but those savings should be passed on to the individual.
 Body clock link? New type of depression could affect millions 
 How to save money on Medicare drug insurance
 The Medicare Prescription Payment Plan is free and open to anyone enrolled in Medicare to help manage out-of-pocket drug costs by spreading total costs across the calendar year. Despite being open to anyone in Medicare, only 5% of people who qualify are enrolled.
 Low-income individuals may qualify for "Extra Help," a program that helps people pay Medicare drug coverage deductibles, coinsurance, premiums and other costs, according to the Medicare website. If you receive Supplemental Security Income payments from Social Security, are enrolled in Medicaid or are enrolled in a state Medicare Savings Program, you will be automatically enrolled in the program.

 You qualify for the program if you are married and make under $32,460, or if you individually make under $23,940.
